# Libraries and path

```{r}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(mc2d)
library(brms)
library(loo)
library(MASS)
library(gsl)

select <- dplyr::select

# Configure graphics device for headless Linux HPC / RStudio server rendering
options(bitmapType = "cairo")
graphics.off()

# Expand R vector memory limit for large 2D Monte Carlo matrices
Sys.setenv(R_MAX_VSIZE = "100Gb")

set.seed(2026)
# Full high-resolution 2D Monte Carlo dimensions (N_V = 10,000 variability x N_U = 2,000 uncertainty)
n_variability <- ndvar(10000)
n_uncertainty <- ndunc(2000)

module1_results_dir <- here("results", "module_01_initial_contamination")
module2_results_dir <- here("results", "module_02_thermal_inactivation")
module3_results_dir <- here("results", "module_03_exposure_assessment")
module4_results_dir <- here("results", "module_04_risk_characterization")
figure_dir <- here("figures")

dir.create(module1_results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(module2_results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(module3_results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(module4_results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(figure_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

This master QMD file connects the full 2D Monte Carlo QMRA pathway across four standard stages:

1. **Module 1: Initial Contamination Distribution:** estimate oyster-level GII prevalence and positive concentration using a Bayesian hurdle model.
2. **Module 2: Process Characterization (Thermal Inactivation):** apply cooking time-temperature profiles to estimate posterior survival fractions $S(U)$.
3. **Module 3: Exposure Assessment:** generate 2D exposure dose matrices $D(V, U)$ ($10,000 \text{ servings} \times 2000 \text{ uncertainty iterations}$) for raw and cooked oysters.
4. **Module 4: Hazard & Risk Characterization:** evaluate the Teunis et al. (2020) hypergeometric dose-response model ($1F1$) and host susceptibility distribution ($P(Se^+)$) directly on 2D exposure matrices $D(V, U)$, summarize risk, perform sensitivity analysis, and estimate annual U.S. illness burden.

# Module 1: Initial Contamination Distribution for Norovirus GII in Oysters

## Purpose

Module 1 estimates the distributions governing pre-cook norovirus GII genome
copies per oyster. It uses a two-part hurdle model fitted to Nishida 2003 and
2007:

1. a pooled global Beta conjugate prevalence model. Following Dr. Arie Havelaar's
   recommendation, commercial market prevalence across Nishida et al. (2003, 2007)
   is pooled across all sampling batches ($k_{\text{total}} = 63$ GII-positive oysters out of
   $n_{\text{total}} = 1,703$ total commercial market oysters sampled), yielding a global
   prevalence distribution $p \sim \operatorname{Beta}(64, 1641)$ with a population mean of
   3.75% (95% CrI: 2.90%–4.71%); and
2. a left-censored positive-concentration model selected by comparing pooled
   Gamma and lognormal distributions for genome copies per oyster conditional
   on GII positivity.

The posterior draws from both models create 500 uncertainty scenarios for prevalence
and positive-concentration parameters. Module 1 establishes the per-oyster baseline
contamination parameters, while individual oyster variability is simulated downstream in Module 3.

## Inputs

```{r module1-inputs}
# GII-positive concentration records from Tables 2 of Nishida 2003 and 2007 (for Concentration Model)
nishida_individual_gii_records <- read_csv(
  here(
    "data", "literature_norovirus_contamination",
    "nishida_individual_gii_records.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

## Prevalence Model
Under a standard non-informative Beta conjugate prior $\operatorname{Beta}(1, 1)$, the posterior prevalence distribution is:

$$
p \sim \operatorname{Beta}(1 + 63, 1 + 1703 - 63) = \operatorname{Beta}(64, 1641)
$$

This pooled global prevalence distribution yields a population mean of **3.75%** (95% CrI: 2.90%–4.71%).

```{r module1-prevalence-pooled}
mc2d_prevalence_node <- mcdata(rbeta(n_uncertainty, shape1 = 64, shape2 = 1641), type = "U")

nishida_prevalence_posterior_summary <- tibble(
  parameter = "Global Pooled Prevalence (P_prev)",
  mean = mean(mc2d_prevalence_node),
  sd = sd(mc2d_prevalence_node),
  median = median(mc2d_prevalence_node),
  lower_2.5 = quantile(mc2d_prevalence_node, 0.025),
  upper_97.5 = quantile(mc2d_prevalence_node, 0.975)
)

nishida_prevalence_posterior_summary

# Clean visualization of Global Pooled Prevalence Beta(64, 1641) distribution
prevalence_plot_df <- tibble(p_prev = c(mc2d_prevalence_node))
p_prev_plot <- ggplot(prevalence_plot_df, aes(x = p_prev)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 40, fill = "#4E79A7", alpha = 0.7, color = "white") +
  geom_density(color = "#2B5C8F", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(c(mc2d_prevalence_node)), linetype = "dashed", color = "#D55E00", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Norovirus GII Prevalence in Market Oysters",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

p_prev_plot
ggsave(
  here("figures", "module1_global_prevalence_distribution.png"),
  p_prev_plot,
  width = 7,
  height = 4,
  dpi = 300
)
ggsave(
  here("figures", "module1_global_prevalence_distribution.tiff"),
  p_prev_plot,
  width = 7,
  height = 4,
  dpi = 300,
  compression = "lzw"
)
```

## Positive-Concentration Model

This model includes only the 63 oysters classified as GII-positive in the
prevalence data. Of these, 22 had quantified concentrations, while 41 were
positive by the qualitative assay but were not quantifiable by the quantitative
assay. These 41 positive observations are represented as left-censored
concentrations, $0 < C \leq 100$ genome copies/oyster. The 1,640 GII-negative
oysters are excluded from the concentration model.

Pooled Gamma and log-normal models are compared by PSIS-LOO on the
original copies/oyster scale. The pooled Gamma candidate is

$$
C\mid C>0 \sim \operatorname{Gamma}(\kappa,\kappa/m),
$$

### Candidate Fits and Model Comparison

```{r module1-concentration-model-comparison}
# Left-censored positive-concentration model.
nishida_concentration_data <- nishida_individual_gii_records %>%
  transmute(
    study_id = factor(study_id, levels = c("Nishida_2003", "Nishida_2007")),
    concentration_gc = if_else(
      censoring == "exact",
      concentration_copies_per_oyster,
      upper_copies_per_oyster
    ),
    censor_code = if_else(censoring == "left_censored", -1L, 0L)
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()

concentration_formula <- bf(
  concentration_gc | cens(censor_code) ~ 1
)
concentration_shape_priors <- c(
  set_prior("normal(6, 4)", class = "Intercept"),
  set_prior("lognormal(0, 1.5)", class = "shape")
)
concentration_lognormal_priors <- c(
  set_prior("normal(6, 4)", class = "Intercept"),
  set_prior("student_t(3, 0, 2)", class = "sigma")
)

module1_results_dir <- here("results", "module_01_initial_contamination")
dir.create(module1_results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

nishida_concentration_gamma_fit <- brm(
  formula = concentration_formula,
  data = nishida_concentration_data,
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  prior = concentration_shape_priors,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  chains = 4,
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 2000,
  cores = 4,
  seed = 1061,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12),
  file = here("results", "module_01_initial_contamination", "nishida_concentration_gamma_fit"),
  silent = 2,
  refresh = 0
)

nishida_concentration_lognormal_fit <- brm(
  formula = concentration_formula,
  data = nishida_concentration_data,
  family = lognormal(),
  prior = concentration_lognormal_priors,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  chains = 4,
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 2000,
  cores = 4,
  seed = 1063,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12),
  file = here("results", "module_01_initial_contamination", "nishida_concentration_lognormal_fit"),
  silent = 2,
  refresh = 0
)

nishida_concentration_loo <- list(
  pooled_gamma = loo::loo(nishida_concentration_gamma_fit),
  pooled_lognormal = loo::loo(nishida_concentration_lognormal_fit)
)
nishida_concentration_model_comparison <-
  loo::loo_compare(nishida_concentration_loo) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  as_tibble(rownames = "model") %>%
  select(model, elpd_diff, se_diff, elpd_loo, se_elpd_loo, looic, se_looic)

nishida_concentration_fit <- nishida_concentration_gamma_fit
nishida_concentration_model_comparison
```

### Gamma Posterior and Diagnostics

```{r module1-concentration-posterior}
nishida_concentration_posterior <-
  posterior::as_draws_df(nishida_concentration_fit) %>%
  transmute(
    posterior_draw = .draw,
    chain = .chain,
    iteration = .iteration,
    positive_mean_gc = exp(b_Intercept),
    concentration_gamma_shape = shape,
    concentration_gamma_cv = 1 / sqrt(shape)
  )

nishida_concentration_fit_summary <- summary(nishida_concentration_fit)
nishida_concentration_parameter_summary <- nishida_concentration_posterior %>%
  transmute(
    positive_mean_gc,
    concentration_gamma_shape,
    concentration_gamma_cv,
    positive_median_gc = qgamma(
      0.5,
      shape = concentration_gamma_shape,
      scale = positive_mean_gc / concentration_gamma_shape
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(parameter) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(value),
    sd = sd(value),
    median = median(value),
    lower_2.5 = quantile(value, 0.025),
    upper_97.5 = quantile(value, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

nishida_concentration_fit_summary
nishida_concentration_parameter_summary
```

### Visual Posterior Predictive Check

```{r module1-concentration-ppc}
nishida_concentration_yrep <- posterior_predict(
  nishida_concentration_fit,
  ndraws = 500
)
nishida_concentration_ppc_draws <- tibble(
  draw = rep(seq_len(nrow(nishida_concentration_yrep)),
             each = ncol(nishida_concentration_yrep)),
  study_id = rep(nishida_individual_gii_records$study_id,
                 times = nrow(nishida_concentration_yrep)),
  concentration_gc = as.vector(t(nishida_concentration_yrep))
) %>%
  group_by(draw, study_id) %>%
  summarise(
    `Fraction <100` = mean(concentration_gc < 100),
    `Median quantified GC/oyster` = median(concentration_gc[concentration_gc >= 100]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(draw, study_id), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value")

nishida_concentration_ppc_intervals <- nishida_concentration_ppc_draws %>%
  group_by(study_id, metric) %>%
  summarise(
    predicted = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    lower = quantile(value, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    upper = quantile(value, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
nishida_concentration_ppc_observed <- nishida_individual_gii_records %>%
  group_by(study_id) %>%
  summarise(
    `Fraction <100` = mean(censoring == "left_censored"),
    `Median quantified GC/oyster` = median(
      concentration_copies_per_oyster[censoring == "exact"]
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(-study_id, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value")

nishida_concentration_pp_check <- ggplot(
  nishida_concentration_ppc_intervals,
  aes(study_id, predicted)
) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), color = "#4E79A7") +
  geom_point(
    data = nishida_concentration_ppc_observed,
    aes(y = value),
    color = "#D55E00",
    shape = 4,
    size = 3
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
    Nishida_2003 = "Nishida 2003",
    Nishida_2007 = "Nishida 2007"
  )) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Blue: posterior-predictive median and 95% interval; orange ×: observed."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

nishida_concentration_pp_check
ggsave(
  here("figures", "module1_positive_concentration_ppc.png"),
  nishida_concentration_pp_check,
  width = 8,
  height = 4,
  dpi = 300
)
ggsave(
  here("figures", "module1_positive_concentration_ppc.tiff"),
  nishida_concentration_pp_check,
  width = 8,
  height = 4,
  dpi = 300,
  compression = "lzw"
)
```


# Module 2: Process Characterization (Thermal Inactivation)

## Purpose

Module 2 supplies posterior uncertainty in thermal survival $S(U)$ for each cooking
condition using the Dynamic Geeraerd model. Pre-cook contamination and serving
variability are not applied here; they are generated in Module 3.

## Dynamic Geeraerd Module Input

```{r}
source(here("scripts", "module2_thermal_functions.R"))
# Primary Baseline Model: Dynamic Geeraerd model (includes 100 °C data)
geeraerd_post <- readRDS(
  here("results", "module_02_thermal_inactivation", "module_02_geeraerd_thermal_kinetics_posterior.rds")
)

# Sensitivity Analysis Scenario Model: Bayesian Meta-Analysis (Shellfish infectivity kinetics posterior)
df_meta_shellfish <- readRDS(
  here("results", "module_02_thermal_inactivation", "module_02_meta_analysis_thermal_kinetics_posterior.rds")
)

df_comeup_updated <- readRDS(
  here("data", "module_02_thermal_inactivation", "df_comeup_updated.rds")
)

# Standard cooking scenario time grid (0 to 16 minutes, every 2 min, covering full sensitivity tail)
module3_cooking_time_grid <- seq(0, 16, by = 2)

steam_excel_path <- here("data", "experimental_temperature_profiles", "Steaming small Cumulative.xlsx")
bake_excel_path  <- here("data", "experimental_temperature_profiles", "Real Oyster Baking cumulative.xlsx")

# 1. Primary Baseline Model (Dynamic Geeraerd) - Steaming & Baking across Small, Medium, Large
module3_cooking_scenarios_geeraerd <- run_module3_cooking_method_size_scenarios(
  post_draws = geeraerd_post,
  steam_path = steam_excel_path,
  bake_path = bake_excel_path,
  model_type = "geeraerd",
  times_min = module3_cooking_time_grid,
  n_unc = n_uncertainty
)
saveRDS(module3_cooking_scenarios_geeraerd, here("results", "module_02_thermal_inactivation", "module_02_cooking_scenarios_geeraerd.rds"))

# 2. Sensitivity Analysis Model (Mafart / Meta-Analysis) - Steaming & Baking across Small, Medium, Large
module3_cooking_scenarios_meta <- run_module3_cooking_method_size_scenarios(
  post_draws = df_meta_shellfish,
  steam_path = steam_excel_path,
  bake_path = bake_excel_path,
  model_type = "mafart",
  times_min = module3_cooking_time_grid,
  n_unc = n_uncertainty
)
saveRDS(module3_cooking_scenarios_meta, here("results", "module_02_thermal_inactivation", "module_02_cooking_scenarios_meta.rds"))

survival_fraction_table_geeraerd <- module3_cooking_scenarios_geeraerd$survival_data
survival_fraction_table_meta <- module3_cooking_scenarios_meta$survival_data

# Convert survival fraction tables into 2D mc2d uncertainty nodes (type = "U", ndunc = 500)
convert_survival_to_mc2d_nodes <- function(survival_df, n_unc = 1000) {
  ndunc(n_unc)
  scenarios <- survival_df %>% dplyr::distinct(method, size, time_min)
  
  node_list <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(scenarios))) {
    m <- scenarios$method[i]
    sz <- scenarios$size[i]
    t_val <- scenarios$time_min[i]
    
    vec_S <- survival_df %>%
      filter(method == m, size == sz, time_min == t_val) %>%
      arrange(uncertainty_iteration) %>%
      pull(survival_fraction)
    
    node_key <- paste(m, sz, paste0(t_val, "min"), sep = "_")
    node_list[[node_key]] <- mcdata(vec_S, type = "U")
  }
  node_list
}

mc2d_survival_nodes_geeraerd <- convert_survival_to_mc2d_nodes(survival_fraction_table_geeraerd, n_unc = n_uncertainty)
mc2d_survival_nodes_meta <- convert_survival_to_mc2d_nodes(survival_fraction_table_meta, n_unc = n_uncertainty)

write_csv(module3_cooking_scenarios_geeraerd$summary_table, here("results", "module_02_thermal_inactivation", "module_02_thermal_survival_summary_geeraerd.csv"))
write_csv(module3_cooking_scenarios_meta$summary_table, here("results", "module_02_thermal_inactivation", "module_02_thermal_survival_summary_meta.csv"))
```

# Module 3: Exposure Assessment

## Purpose

Module 3 combines the pre-harvest initial contamination $GC_{\text{precook}}(V, U)$ with the size-stratified thermal survival nodes $S(U)$ from Module 2. 

In strict adherence to QMRA principles, **Initial contamination is sampled independently from oyster size**, establishing the baseline population-average exposure. The physical variation of oyster size (**Small, Medium, Large**) operates directly through the size-stratified thermal inactivation kinetics $S_{\text{size}}(U)$ for both **Steaming** and **Baking** scenarios.

Module 3 produces 2D per-oyster post-cook residual dose matrices $GC_{\text{postcook, size}}(V, U)$ (in Genome Copies / Infectious Units per oyster). Serving aggregation (6 and 12 oysters) and post-hoc random permutation size mixing are evaluated downstream in Module 4.

## Individual Oyster Pre-Cook & Post-Cook Dose Generation

```{r}
# Read Global Pooled Prevalence mc2d Uncertainty Node (type = "U", dimension: 2000)
prevalence_selected_u <- c(mc2d_prevalence_node)

# Left-Censored Bayesian Gamma Concentration model draws
concentration_selected <- nishida_concentration_posterior[
  sample.int(nrow(nishida_concentration_posterior), n_uncertainty),
]

# Generate per-oyster pre-cook contamination matrix
# Biological conversion: Multiply raw qPCR genome copies
# Reference ratio range from Mirmahdi et al. (2025) "Navigating uncertainties in RT-qPCR and plaque assay for infectivity assessment of norovirus":
# 2.5% to 97.5% log10 GC:PFU coverage is [3.39, 4.22] (linear: [2455, 16596]), median is 3.7 log10 (~5012:1).
infectious_dose_precook_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = n_variability, ncol = n_uncertainty)

log10_q_inv_min <- 3.39 # log10(2455), 2.5th percentile lower bound from Mirmahdi et al. (2025)
log10_q_inv_max <- 4.22 # log10(16596), 97.5th percentile upper bound from Mirmahdi et al. (2025)
q_inv_u <- 10^runif(n_uncertainty, min = log10_q_inv_min, max = log10_q_inv_max)
q_u <- 1 / q_inv_u

for (u in seq_len(n_uncertainty)) {
  p_prev_u <- prevalence_selected_u[u]
  positive <- rbinom(n_variability, size = 1, prob = p_prev_u) == 1
  
  raw_gc <- rgamma(
    sum(positive),
    shape = concentration_selected$concentration_gamma_shape[u],
    scale = concentration_selected$positive_mean_gc[u] / concentration_selected$concentration_gamma_shape[u]
  )
  
  # Convert raw qPCR copies to initial bioavailable infectious virions (Effective GC / Virions)
  infectious_dose_precook_matrix[positive, u] <- raw_gc * q_u[u]
}

infectious_dose_precook_node <- mcdata(infectious_dose_precook_matrix, type = "VU")
saveRDS(infectious_dose_precook_node, here("results", "module_03_exposure_assessment", "infectious_dose_precook_node.rds"))

# Calculate per-oyster post-cook residual doses across cooking scenarios and size classes
calculate_per_oyster_postcook_node <- function(precook_node, survival_node) {
  precook_node * survival_node
}

# 1. Primary Baseline Model (Dynamic Geeraerd) - Per-oyster residual dose nodes
mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd <- map(mc2d_survival_nodes_geeraerd, function(s_node) {
  calculate_per_oyster_postcook_node(infectious_dose_precook_node, s_node)
})
saveRDS(mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd, here("results", "module_03_exposure_assessment", "mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd.rds"))

# 2. Sensitivity Model (Mafart / Meta-Analysis) - Per-oyster residual dose nodes
mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta <- map(mc2d_survival_nodes_meta, function(s_node) {
  calculate_per_oyster_postcook_node(infectious_dose_precook_node, s_node)
})
saveRDS(mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta, here("results", "module_03_exposure_assessment", "mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta.rds"))

# Scenario Condition Grid for Module 4 risk iteration
condition_grid <- survival_fraction_table_geeraerd %>%
  distinct(method, size, time_min) %>%
  arrange(method, size, time_min)
saveRDS(condition_grid, here("results", "module_03_exposure_assessment", "condition_grid.rds"))

# Export Module 3 Pre-Cook & Post-Cook Exposure Assessment Summaries
precook_dose_summary <- tibble(
  metric = c("Mean Precook Dose (Virions/oyster)", "Median Precook Dose", "P95 Precook Dose", "P99 Precook Dose"),
  value = c(
    mean(infectious_dose_precook_matrix),
    median(infectious_dose_precook_matrix),
    quantile(infectious_dose_precook_matrix, 0.95),
    quantile(infectious_dose_precook_matrix, 0.99)
  )
)
write_csv(precook_dose_summary, here("results", "module_03_exposure_assessment", "module_03_per_oyster_precook_exposure_summary.csv"))

# Per-oyster Post-Cook Exposure Summaries across all cooking conditions
summarize_postcook_dose_nodes <- function(postcook_nodes) {
  map_dfr(names(postcook_nodes), function(node_key) {
    node_mat <- unclass(postcook_nodes[[node_key]])[, , 1]
    parts <- strsplit(node_key, "_")[[1]]
    m_val <- parts[1]
    sz_val <- parts[2]
    t_val <- as.numeric(gsub("min", "", parts[3]))
    
    tibble(
      method = m_val,
      size = sz_val,
      time_min = t_val,
      mean_postcook_virions_per_oyster = mean(node_mat),
      median_postcook_virions_per_oyster = median(node_mat),
      p95_postcook_virions_per_oyster = quantile(node_mat, 0.95),
      p99_postcook_virions_per_oyster = quantile(node_mat, 0.99)
    )
  }) %>%
    arrange(method, size, time_min)
}

postcook_exposure_summary_geeraerd <- summarize_postcook_dose_nodes(mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd)
postcook_exposure_summary_meta     <- summarize_postcook_dose_nodes(mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta)

write_csv(postcook_exposure_summary_geeraerd, here("results", "module_03_exposure_assessment", "module_03_per_oyster_postcook_exposure_summary_geeraerd.csv"))
write_csv(postcook_exposure_summary_meta, here("results", "module_03_exposure_assessment", "module_03_per_oyster_postcook_exposure_summary_meta.csv"))
```


# Module 4: Hazard & Risk Characterization

## Purpose

Module 4 receives the 2D per-oyster exposure dose matrices from Module 3, constructs 6-oyster and 12-oyster mixed servings (with post-hoc size mixing across Small, Medium, and Large oysters), and evaluates infection and illness risk per serving.

Dose-response risk is evaluated using the **Teunis et al. (2020)** Kummer hypergeometric dose-response model ($1F1$) parameterized for Norovirus GII ($Se^+$):

$$P_{\text{inf}}(D \mid Se^+) = 1 - {}_1F_1(\alpha, \alpha + \beta, -D)$$
$$P_{\text{ill|inf}}(D \mid Se^+) = 1 - (1 + D / \eta)^{-\rho}$$

Host susceptibility is represented by a Beta distribution fitted to Messner et al. (2014) (mean 0.72, 95% CrI 0.63–0.80):

$$P(Se^+) \sim \operatorname{Beta}(\alpha_{\text{se}}, \beta_{\text{se}})$$

## Risk Characterization & Model Sensitivity Analysis

Module 4 evaluates infection and illness risk per serving using the **Teunis et al. (2020)** Kummer hypergeometric dose-response model ($1F1$) and Messner et al. (2014) host secretor susceptibility $P(Se^+)$.

Risk is evaluated for both:
1. **Baseline Primary Model**: Dynamic Geeraerd model (fitted with 100°C experimental data).
2. **Sensitivity Analysis Model**: Systematic Review Bayesian Meta-Analysis model (Mafart model with shellfish parameters $D_{60} = 4.30\text{ min}, z = 30.10^\circ\text{C}, \beta = 0.39$).

```{r module4-teunis-risk-evaluation}
source(here("scripts", "module4_risk_characterization_functions.R"))
```

## Simulation Numerical Convergence Assessment

Prior to interpreting risk characterization results, numerical convergence was verified across both **Variability ($N_{\text{variability}} = 10,000$)** and **Uncertainty ($N_{\text{uncertainty}} = 2,000$)** dimensions to ensure stability of population risk estimates.

```{r module4-simulation-convergence-assessment}
infectious_dose_precook_node <- readRDS(here("results", "module_03_exposure_assessment", "infectious_dose_precook_node.rds"))

# Assess numerical stability of Mean P(illness) across N_var and N_unc
conv_res <- assess_simulation_convergence(
  precook_node = infectious_dose_precook_node,
  sizes_var = c(500, 1000, 2500, 5000, 10000),
  sizes_unc = c(50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000)
)

# Export Convergence Data
write_csv(conv_res, here("results", "module_04_risk_characterization", "module4_numerical_convergence_data.csv"))

# Plot Convergence Curves
plot_simulation_convergence(conv_res, here("figures", "module4_numerical_convergence_plot.png"))

conv_res
```

## Regional Sensitivity Analysis: Monte Carlo Filtering (MCF)

Monte Carlo Filtering (MCF) partitions simulation iterations into two distinct groups based on the **safety cutoff threshold ($P_{\text{illness}} = 10^{-4}$, 0.01% per serving)**:
1. **Unsafe Group ($B$)**: Iterations where illness risk $P_{\text{illness}} \ge 10^{-4}$ (High-Risk / Outbreak Conditions).
2. **Safe Group ($\bar{B}$)**: Iterations where illness risk $P_{\text{illness}} < 10^{-4}$ (FDA/QMRA Benchmark Compliant).

Note: Under updated infectivity parameters ($Q \sim 2455 - 16596$), raw oyster baseline risk is $\approx 3.8 \times 10^{-4}$. Therefore, setting cutoff $= 10^{-4}$ provides a responsive cutoff that properly categorizes raw and undercooked oysters as high-risk ($P \ge 10^{-4}$).

Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) tests quantify parameter sensitivity to identify critical drivers of exceeding the safety threshold ($P_{\text{illness}} \ge 10^{-4}$).

```{r module4-monte-carlo-filtering}
mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd <- readRDS(here("results", "module_03_exposure_assessment", "mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd.rds"))
mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta     <- readRDS(here("results", "module_03_exposure_assessment", "mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta.rds"))

# Run Monte Carlo Filtering for Representative Baseline Scenario (Steaming Medium 4 min)
mcf_result <- run_monte_carlo_filtering(
  postcook_nodes_list = mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd,
  cutoff = 0.0001
)

# Export KS Test Results
write_csv(mcf_result$ks_table, here("results", "module_04_risk_characterization", "module4_mcf_ks_test_results.csv"))

# Plot Empirical CDF Comparison Curves for Top Critical Parameter
plot_mcf_cdf_curves(mcf_result, here("figures", "module4_mcf_cdf_top_parameter.png"))

# 1. Run Monte Carlo Filtering Loop across all scenarios - Primary Baseline Model (Geeraerd)
mcf_matrix_geeraerd <- run_mcf_scenario_matrix(
  postcook_nodes_list = mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd,
  cutoff = 0.0001
)
write_csv(mcf_matrix_geeraerd, here("results", "module_04_risk_characterization", "module4_mcf_scenario_safety_matrix.csv"))
write_csv(mcf_matrix_geeraerd, here("results", "module_04_risk_characterization", "module4_mcf_scenario_safety_matrix_geeraerd.csv"))

# 2. Run Monte Carlo Filtering Loop across all scenarios - Sensitivity Model (Meta-Analysis)
mcf_matrix_meta <- run_mcf_scenario_matrix(
  postcook_nodes_list = mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta,
  cutoff = 0.0001
)
write_csv(mcf_matrix_meta, here("results", "module_04_risk_characterization", "module4_mcf_scenario_safety_matrix_meta.csv"))

mcf_matrix_geeraerd
```
